title: Refute the arbitrary-ideal link Nullstellensatz (10400049)
body:
This PR answers Bar-Natan’s Problem2.27 negatively for arbitrary ideals in the ordinary uncompleted characteristic-zero algebra of all finite-order link invariants, with actual links as zeros. For g=sum of squared pairwise linking numbers and I=g(4g-1)V, the zero set is the nonempty algebraically split locus, while g is outside radical(I). The singular full-twist argument supplies a character on the entire finite-order algebra, not merely C[g]. The separate indexed linking-number-generated ideal in the labelled theory remains undecided.

Preprint and verification archive: [10.5281/zenodo.23331295](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23331295). The exact reviewed PDF, LaTeX source and standalone verification package are published as version1.0. The DOI tracker entry is 'Math Puzzles'!A70:D70.

The polynomiality methods are older and explicitly credited to Stanford–Trapp, Eisermann and Stoimenow. The bounded primary-body priority audit located no explicit equivalent counterexample in the inspected bodies and discloses uninspected final-version/body limits. No historical firstness, guaranteed novelty, new polynomiality method or contemporaneous-independence claim is made.

Three mathematical adversary families, full-source priority checks, Root reproduction and two successive fresh whole-publication-package reviews are recorded in draft_pr_publication_program_20260930/audits/pr177_10400049. Review01’s three minor clarifications were propagated globally; the new review02 found no substantive or minor issue. The explicitly guarded verification scripts pass normally and with optimization; deliberate wrong-science controls are rejected. Finite diagnostics supplement the written universal proof.

AI tools were used extensively in development, drafting, verification and adversarial review. This preprint is unrefereed and has not undergone conventional human peer review.

Repository integration will preserve the original submitted head as a merge parent, retain original artifacts as labelled history, and install current scientific copies identical to publication_package_v2.
